text:
elaine: Heads-up — I opened a docs PR to add an embedding pricing example + a small SDK snippet for the tiered billing page. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/8341 :eyes:

sam: Thanks! linking the PR — can you paste the exact example you want? I can help convert to python/go snippets.

elaine: Short copy below. We want a worked example showing how embedding units map to pricing tiers and how the dashboard shows units consumed. Also include a quick python snippet using the new sdk client:```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
# embeddings cost measured in embedding_units
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="open-embed-small", input=["hello world"])
print(resp.data[0].vector[:6])
```

sam: Nice. Two tiny asks: 1) the anchor id in the tiering doc was changed last week, so links in the PR are failing doc-lint. 2) Can you add a short note that enterprise customers can opt for reserved capacity pricing (per-month) vs unit-based?

elaine: Good catch on the anchor. I'll update. And yes add one sentence about reserved capacity.

docs-bot: doc-lint reported: link-check failed for https://docs.redwood.ai/pricing#embedding-tiers -> 404. See CI log: https://ci.redwood.ai/12345/logs/5678

ben: For the dashboard bit — I can add a sample Grafana panel query for embedding_units. Suggest metric name: `redwood.billing.embedding_units_total` with labels {org_id}. Want me to push that to the snippet?

mike: From billing side: confirm that "embedding_units" aggregated by month is what the pricing calc uses. Seat-based tiers are separate; we should avoid mixing both in the same example. Maybe show a short table: 1k units = $0.10, 10k = $0.9, 100k = $8.0 (placeholder).

sam: I pushed a quick python + go pair to the PR, also fixed the anchor. Go snippet (short):```go
client := redwood.NewClient(nil)
resp, _ := client.Embeddings.Create(context.Background(), redwood.EmbeddingsCreateParams{Model: "open-embed-small", Input: []string{"hello world"}})
fmt.Println(resp.Data[0].Vector[:5])
```

ben: Added panel JSON to the PR under `/_includes/dashboard_examples/embedding_panel.json`. Query uses `sum(increase(redwood_billing_embedding_units_total[30d])) by (org_id)`. Left a short comment in the PR about timezone and month boundaries.

elaine: Amazing — CI is re-running. @docs-bot can you re-check? :pray:

docs-bot: Re-run complete — doc-lint passed. No broken links.

mike: Quick product-nit: in the worked example, call out that batching and prefix caching can reduce per-unit consumption so customers know why their dashboard might show lower units than raw requests.

elaine: Added one sentence about batching and cache impact. I also updated the pricing table with numbers from finance and added reserved capacity sentence.

sam: LGTM, small markdown lint nit fixed.

ben: CI + grafana snippet look good from my side. Also added a short note in the snippet about org_id label and account timezone.

elaine: Cool — merging now. Will cherry-pick to the 1.2 release branch after the merge. Thanks everyone :shipit:
